50 working days. Every milestone is an offset from the festival date, so =WORKDAY(DATE(2026,11,8),-40) gives 14 September for a vendor order that needs eight weeks of lead time, and if Nandini moves the campaign a week, the whole plan moves with it.

=DATE(2025,10,20)-XLOOKUP(8,Campaigns!A:A,Campaigns!F:F)

−5: Big Diwali Dhamaka 2025 ended on 25 October, five days after the festival, having started on 10 October — only ten days before it. The 2024 campaign started twelve days before Diwali and ran until 5 November. That is the "what went wrong" note, in two cells.

=SUMIFS(Sales!P:P,Sales!Q:Q,"Delivered",Sales!B:B,">="&DATE(2025,10,1),Sales!B:B,"<="&DATE(2025,11,30))
 /SUMIFS(Sales!P:P,Sales!Q:Q,"Delivered",Sales!B:B,">="&DATE(2025,1,1),Sales!B:B,"<="&DATE(2025,12,31))

23 per cent of the year in two months, which is the number that goes at the top of the project brief and justifies the hub existing.

The first three build steps, which the Lab does not run.

  1. Teams ▸ Teams ▸ Create team ▸ From scratch ▸ Private. Name it Diwali 2026 Launch, add the five channels, and in each channel's Files ▸ Open in SharePoint create the folder structure: 01_Plan, 02_Creative, 03_Stock, 04_Store-Readiness, 99_Archive.
  2. Planner ▸ New plan ▸ Add to an existing team and pick the team. Create the four buckets, then Add task for each milestone with the due date typed from your sheet, an assignee, and a label. Switch to Schedule view and check nothing lands on a weekend or on Diwali itself.
  3. In the General channel ▸ New conversation ▸ Loop component ▸ Table. Five columns: Workstream, Status, Next milestone, Date, Owner. Post it, then open the same component from Loop app and edit a cell to prove it syncs.
@and(less(item()?['dueDateTime'], utcNow()), less(item()?['percentComplete'], 100))

Watch out

The trap is in the calendar, and the workbook proves it. Diwali moved from 1 November 2024 to 20 October 2025 and moves again to 8 November 2026, so every date in a copied plan is wrong by two to three weeks; the campaign windows in Campaigns show exactly what that did last year, when the 2025 TV campaign started ten days before the festival and the 2024 one twelve, neither of which is a festive-season run-up. Check: =XLOOKUP(8,Campaigns!A:A,Campaigns!E:E)-XLOOKUP(4,Campaigns!A:A,Campaigns!E:E) is 355 days: the 2025 campaign started ten days earlier in the calendar than 2024's, for a festival that came twelve days earlier, so it had two days less run-up. Twelve days and ten days before the festival are both too late, and both plans were carried forward by calendar date instead of being built back from the festival. Second: the stock workstream starts from 235 store-product lines below reorder level on 31 August and 51 of them are discontinued products (see capstone 06); a Planner task that says "reorder everything below level" is wrong before it is assigned. Third, in the tools: Planner has no dependencies, so a slipped vendor order does not move the stock-in-store date by itself — your sheet does that, and the flow has to re-post the dates; and a Loop component lives in the OneDrive of whoever posted it, so post it from the team owner's account or it disappears when the trainee leaves.

The deliverable

  • The live hub: a Team with five channels, the SharePoint library with the folder structure and the naming convention applied, the Planner plan with every milestone dated and owned, the Loop status in General, both flows exported as .zip, all linked from a README.docx pinned in General.
  • 2026-09_Launch-Plan_v01.xlsx: the milestone sheet built backwards from the festival date with WORKDAY, the Assumptions sheet of offsets, the stock opening position from Inventory with discontinued lines excluded, and the store-readiness checklist for twelve stores.
  • Diwali-2025-Lessons.docx: one page, the campaign dates against the festival dates, the season's share of revenue, and three things that change in 2026, each of which is a dated task in Planner.

Stretch goals

  • Add a Microsoft List for store issues with a rule that emails the workstream owner when priority is High, and connect it to the Planner flow.
  • Build a Power Automate approval for creative sign-off with a two-day reminder, and log the approvals to a SharePoint list.
  • Produce a Gantt-style view of the milestone sheet with conditional formatting on a week grid, and compare it with Planner's Schedule view.
CriterionWeightWhat full marks looks like
Plan built backwards25%Every milestone an offset from the festival date via WORKDAY; offsets on Assumptions; moving the date moves the plan; nothing lands on a weekend.
Hub structure20%Team, channels, folders and Planner buckets mirror the workstreams; Files tabs point at the right SharePoint folders; naming convention followed.
Automation20%Both flows run in the test log; overdue post @mentions the right owner; a Forms issue becomes a Planner task in the right bucket within a minute.
Trap handling20%The moving festival date, the discontinued-stock lines and the Planner/Loop ownership limits all named and handled in the plan.
Running the week15%One weekly review run entirely from the hub: agenda in the invite, Loop status as the document, follow-ups as tasks, no status email sent.

Turning a capstone into a portfolio piece

A finished project and a portfolio piece are different objects. The first is work; the second is work that a stranger can evaluate in ninety seconds without your help. The gap between them is mostly writing, and a little bit of file hygiene.

The folder

Open the folder as a stranger. The README is the first thing listed, the workbook is the second, the deck or document is the third, nothing else is at the top level. Every file follows YYYY-MM_Project-Name_vNN. The workbook opens on the README sheet, not on a raw data sheet, and the first thing on it is the question and the answer. The deck opens on a title slide with the recommendation on it. If a reviewer has to hunt, you have already lost half of the ninety seconds.

The README

Six sections, in this order, under a page and a half of scroll.

  1. The question and who asked it. Two sentences. "The COO had one refurbishment budget and eleven store managers asking for it."
  2. The answer. At the top, before the method. Three sentences with numbers in them.
  3. The data. Which sheets, what one row means in each, the date range and the as-of date.
  4. Definitions. What revenue means here, what "delivered" means here, what you excluded and why. Experienced reviewers read this section first.
  5. Method and files. A paragraph, then which sheet or slide holds what. Name the tools honestly: "PivotTable with a slicer, reconciled with SUMIFS on the Checks sheet."
  6. Caveats. The trap you handled, the sample limitation, what you would do with better data.

The 90-second version

Interviewers ask about projects to find out whether you can think, not whether you can recall a ribbon path. Four beats, out loud.

Situation (15 seconds)
Who needed what, and what decision was waiting. "The CFO wanted a monthly pack that would not need rebuilding every month."
The definition you chose (20 seconds)
The judgement call and why. "Revenue could be all statuses or delivered only. I used delivered, and I reported returns one month in arrears because they land a median of nine days after the order."
The trap you caught (25 seconds)
The best thirty seconds you have. "August looked 36 per cent up on July. Thirteen orders were still Processing and the returns had not landed. I labelled the month provisional and showed the same-month-last-year comparison instead."
The recommendation (20 seconds)
What you told them and what would change it. "Electronics carried the month. The delivered figure already excludes the Processing orders, so if they all cancel nothing changes; if August's returns land at July's size the month is still up about 30 per cent."

Practise it against a clock. Ninety seconds is much shorter than it feels, and the most common failure is spending sixty of them describing which sheets the workbook has.

In the interview

Bring the workbook on a laptop and offer to open it. Most candidates cannot, because the file only works on the machine it was built on. Yours refreshes cleanly, the Checks sheet is green, and the interviewer will click on one formula to see if you wrote it. Make that formula a good one — the XLOOKUP that removed the discontinued products, or the SORTBY spill behind the dashboard — and be ready to explain it in a sentence.

Practice · Live workbook

Formula Lab

A formula bar wired to the full Novamart workbook. Type any Excel formula, run it with Ctrl+Enter, and click a column in the sheet panel to drop its reference into your formula. Everything spills, nothing needs saving, and you cannot break anything.

Editor

Novamart workbook

Working in here

Ctrl+Enter (or Cmd+Enter) runs whatever is in the editor. A formula can span several lines; Excel ignores the line breaks and so does the Lab. The leading = is optional but you should type it anyway, out of habit. Your last formula is kept in this browser between visits.

References work the way they do in Excel: Sales!P:P is a whole column, Stores!B2:B14 is a bounded range, $A$1 is fine, and a sheet with a space in its name would be quoted with single quotes (none of ours have one). Row 1 of every sheet is the header, which matters for COUNTA and for anything you do with whole columns.

Pro habit

Build a long formula from the inside out and run it after each layer. Get UNIQUE(Sales!K2:K6315) spilling six categories before you wrap it in SUMIFS, and get the SUMIFS column right before you wrap that in SORTBY. A wrong number at the end is much harder to find than a wrong list in the middle.

Things worth trying

  • Run =SUM(Sales!P:P), then =SUMIFS(Sales!P:P,Sales!Q:Q,"Delivered"), and look at the gap. That is cancelled and returned revenue, and Module 03 is about why the second number is the one you report.
  • Copy any formula from a module with its Lab button, then change one argument and predict the result before you run it.
  • Try a deliberately wrong one: =VLOOKUP("Kochi",Stores!B:C,2,FALSE). It returns #N/A because Kochi is a city, not a store name. Module 04 is about reading that error correctly.
  • Ask it for a spill: =SORT(UNIQUE(Sales!K2:K6315)). The result panel shows the array the way Excel would fill it down the sheet.

What the Lab can and cannot run

It runs the functions below, with Excel 365 semantics, against the workbook you can see in the preview. It does not run structured references (Table1[Revenue]), PivotTables, Power Query, DAX, VBA or anything that needs a workbook of your own; those are shown on the module pages as reference syntax with a "syntax" badge. TODAY() is pinned to 31 August 2026, the dataset's as-of date. Click a function to insert it.

Reference · Print-friendly

Microsoft 365 cheat sheet

Everything this course teaches, on a few printed pages, in the order a week at Novamart uses it: get the data in, make it a Table, summarise it, show it, write it up, send it, and let a flow do it next time. Keep it beside you for the first month on the job. By month two you'll only need the habits list at the end.

Excel: the keys and the grid

Windows shortcuts. On a Mac, Ctrl is usually ⌘, F4 is ⌘+T, and Alt key tips don't exist; everything else below works the same.

Moving and selecting

Ctrl+Arrow
Jump to the edge of the data block. Ctrl+Down on a column finds where the data really ends.
Ctrl+Shift+Arrow
Select to the edge. The way to grab 6,314 rows without scrolling.
Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End
A1, or the last used cell. If Ctrl+End lands far below your data, there's a stray value or formatting to clear.
Ctrl+A
Select the current block; press twice for the whole sheet.
Ctrl+G ▸ Special ▸ Blanks
Select every blank cell in a range. Type a value, Ctrl+Enter to fill them all.

Editing

F2
Edit the cell in place; the coloured reference boxes show you what a formula points at.
F4
While editing, cycles a reference: A1 → $A$1 → A$1 → $A1. After editing, repeats your last action.
F9
Select part of a formula in edit mode and press F9 to see its value. Esc to undo before it sticks.
Ctrl+1
Format Cells. Indian rupee format: [>=10000000]₹##\,##\,##\,##0;[>=100000]₹##\,##\,##0;₹##,##0, or just #,##,##0.
Alt+=
AutoSum. Check the range it guessed before you press Enter.
Ctrl+;
Today's date as a value (not a formula). Ctrl+Shift+; for the time.
Ctrl+E
Flash Fill. Type two examples, Excel finishes the column. Check the whole column; it guesses.

Sheets, panes and paste

Ctrl+T
Make a Table. Do this before anything else.
View ▸ Freeze Panes ▸ Top Row
Header stays put. Freeze the first column too when a sheet is wide.
Ctrl+Shift+L
Filter arrows on / off.
Ctrl+Alt+V
Paste Special. Values (kills formulas, keeps numbers), Transpose, Formats.
Ctrl+H
Find and Replace. Replace * with nothing to strip text after a character; tick "Match entire cell contents" to avoid partial hits.
Ctrl+`
Show every formula instead of its result. Best way to audit a sheet you inherited.
Formulas ▸ Evaluate Formula
Step through a formula one calculation at a time.

Tables, references and the tidy rules

Excel Tables

Ctrl+T, then Table Design ▸ Table Name
Name it tSales, tStores. Unnamed Tables are called Table1, Table2, and nobody knows which is which.
=[@Qty]*[@UnitPrice]
This row's cells. Type once, it fills the column and follows new rows.
=SUM(tSales[LineRevenue])
A whole column by name. Survives inserted rows and columns.
Table Design ▸ Total Row
Adds SUBTOTAL(109,…), which ignores filtered-out rows. A plain SUM doesn't.
Table Design ▸ Insert Slicer
Click-to-filter buttons for a Table, not just a pivot.

References

A1
Relative: shifts when copied.
$A$1
Absolute: a rate, a target, a date everyone points at.
A$1 / $A1
Mixed: lock the row for a header, the column for a label. The engine of a two-way grid.
Sales!P:P
A whole column on another sheet. Fine in SUMIFS; slow in array formulas, so bound them (P2:P6315).
Formulas ▸ Define Name
AsOfDate, GSTRate. Named cells read like English and never move.
# after a cell: =SUM(F2#)
The whole spilled range that starts at F2.

Tidy data, the six rules

One header row
Row 1, short names, no merged cells, no units in the header ("Revenue" not "Revenue (₹ lakh)").
One record per row
One order line per row. Never a subtotal row inside the data.
One value per cell
"Delhi, North" is two columns.
Numbers are numbers
The green triangle means text. VALUE() or Text to Columns fixes a whole column.
Dates are dates
Right-aligned and ISNUMBER is TRUE. "13/07/2026" as text sorts wrong and sums to nothing.
No blank rows or columns
They break Ctrl+Arrow, Tables and pivots. Blanks inside a column are fine and mean "unknown".

Formula patterns

The SUMIFS family

=SUMIFS(sum, range1, crit1, range2, crit2)
Sum with AND-ed conditions. Sum range first. COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS, MINIFS take the same pairs.
"Delivered" · "<>Cancelled"
Equal, not equal. Case doesn't matter.
">="&DATE(2026,8,1)
A date bound. Always two of them for a range, and the second is "<=" the last day.
"Elec*" · "*Kochi*" · "2025-*"
Wildcards: starts with, contains, a whole year of "YYYY-MM".
"" · "<>"
Blank, not blank. Pair a whole-column blank test with a never-blank column: COUNTIFS(A:A,"<>",C:C,"").
SUMIFS(P:P, K:K, UNIQUE(K2:K6315))
An array of criteria spills one total per value. The pivot-in-a-formula.
SUMPRODUCT((F2:F6315="South")*(Q2:Q6315="Delivered")*P2:P6315)
Same as SUMIFS but takes OR logic and calculated tests. Slower.

Lookups

=XLOOKUP(key, lookup_col, return_col, "not found")
Exact match by default, looks any direction, returns a message instead of #N/A.
=XLOOKUP(key, A:A, B:D)
Return several columns at once; they spill.
=XLOOKUP(key, A:A, D:D, , 0, -1)
Search from the bottom: the latest row for a key.
=XLOOKUP(amount, slab_from, rate, , -1)
Next smaller item: GST slabs, commission bands. Slab table sorted ascending.
=INDEX(return_col, MATCH(key, lookup_col, 0))
Works in every Excel since 1993. Two-way: INDEX(grid, MATCH(row), MATCH(col)).
=VLOOKUP(key, table, col_num, FALSE)
Legacy. The FALSE is not optional. Breaks when a column is inserted; can't look left.
=IFNA(XLOOKUP(...), 0)
Trap only #N/A. IFERROR hides every error, including your typos.
=COUNTIF(other_list, key)=0
"Is this key missing from the other list?" Reconciliation in one column.

Dynamic arrays

=UNIQUE(range)
Distinct values, in first-seen order. Wrap in SORT for alphabetical.
=FILTER(range, condition, "none")
Rows that pass. Combine conditions with * (AND) and + (OR).
=SORT(array, col, -1) · =SORTBY(array, key_col, -1)
Sort by a column inside the array, or by a column outside it.
=TAKE(array, 5) · =TAKE(array, -5)
First five rows, last five rows. Top-N is SORT then TAKE.
=HSTACK(a, b) · =VSTACK(a, b)
Glue arrays side by side or one under the other: labels next to totals.
=SEQUENCE(12)
1 to 12. EDATE(start, SEQUENCE(12)-1) is a month spine.
#SPILL!
Something is in the way below or to the right. Clear it or move the formula.

Dates

=TODAY()
Recalculates every day. For a report, put the as-of date in a named cell instead.
=DATE(2026,8,1)
Build a date from parts. Never type "1/8/2026" into a formula.
=EOMONTH(d, 0) · =EOMONTH(d, -1)+1
Last day of d's month; first day of it.
=EDATE(d, -12)
Same day last year. The basis of every YoY column.
=TEXT(d, "yyyy-mm")
A month key that sorts correctly. "dd-mmm-yyyy" for display.
=DATEDIF(start, end, "M")
Whole months between. "Y" for years, "D" for days. Undocumented, works everywhere.
=NETWORKDAYS(start, end, holidays)
Working days, Mon–Fri less a holiday list. WORKDAY(start, n) goes the other way.

Text clean-up

=PROPER(TRIM(A2))
" MOHIT RAO " → "Mohit Rao". TRIM removes doubled and edge spaces.
=LOWER(TRIM(email))
Normalise before you dedupe. "A@x.com" and "a@x.com" are one person.
=CLEAN(A2)
Removes non-printing characters that TRIM can't see. SUBSTITUTE(A2, CHAR(160), "") for the web's non-breaking space.
=TEXTBEFORE(email, "@") · =TEXTAFTER(email, "@")
Split at a marker without counting characters.
=TEXTSPLIT(A2, ",")
One cell into many. TEXTJOIN(", ", TRUE, range) puts them back.
=LEFT(A2, 3) · =RIGHT(A2, 4) · =MID(A2, 4, 2) · =LEN(A2)
Slice by position. LEN before and after TRIM tells you how many spaces you removed.
=SUBSTITUTE(phone, " ", "")
Strip a character everywhere. REPLACE works by position instead.

Logic, errors and LET

=IF(test, yes, no)
Two outcomes. Three or more: IFS(t1, r1, t2, r2, TRUE, else).
=AND(a, b) · =OR(a, b)
Inside IF. Both true; either true.
=IFERROR(x, "")
Last resort. Prefer IFNA for lookups so real errors still show.
#N/A · #VALUE! · #DIV/0! · #REF! · #NAME? · #SPILL!
Not found · wrong type (text in maths) · zero denominator · deleted cell · misspelled function or missing quotes · blocked spill.
=LET(rev, SUMIFS(...), n, COUNTIFS(...), rev/n)
Name the parts, use them once, read the formula six months later.
=LAMBDA(x, x*1.18) via Define Name
Your own function: =WithGST(price). Define it once in Name Manager.

PivotTable moves

Build

Click in the Table ▸ Insert ▸ PivotTable ▸ New Worksheet
From a Table, so Refresh picks up new rows.
Rows · Columns · Values · Filters
What goes down the side; across the top; the number; the page filter. Say the grain: "one row per store".
Value Field Settings ▸ Summarize by
Sum for money, Count for rows, Average with the count beside it. Count of lines is not count of orders.
Show Values As
% of Column Total, % of Parent Row, Running Total, Difference From (previous month). The YoY column is "% Difference From, Year, previous".
Right-click a date ▸ Group
Months, Quarters, Years together. Excel 365 groups automatically; ungroup if you need days.
PivotTable Analyze ▸ Insert Slicer / Timeline
Click filters for a dashboard. Report Connections links one slicer to many pivots.

Shape and use

Design ▸ Report Layout ▸ Tabular + Repeat All Item Labels
A flat grid you can VLOOKUP against or copy into another analysis.
Design ▸ Subtotals ▸ Do Not Show
For a clean export. Grand Totals off too, or someone sums the sum.
Row label dropdown ▸ Value Filters ▸ Top 10
Top-N inside the pivot. Sort ▸ More Sort Options for sort by value.
Right-click ▸ Refresh · Data ▸ Refresh All
New rows in the source don't appear until you do this. The cause of most "stale numbers".
=GETPIVOTDATA("LineRevenue", $A$3, "Store", "Novamart Kothrud")
Pull one pivot cell by name into a report; survives the pivot being re-sorted.
Fields, Items & Sets ▸ Calculated Field
Sums then calculates; average-of-averages trap. Use a Data Model measure instead (Module 13).

Power Query steps

Get and shape

Data ▸ Get Data ▸ From Text/CSV · From Workbook · From Folder · From Web · From SharePoint Folder
Point at the source once. From Folder appends every file in it, and next month's file just works.
Home ▸ Use First Row as Headers
Then check every column's type icon. ABC is text, 123 is number, calendar is date.
Transform ▸ Data Type ▸ Using Locale
Parse "13/07/2026" as English (India). Mixed formats: split into two queries or add a conditional column.
Transform ▸ Format ▸ Trim · Clean · Capitalize Each Word · lowercase
The Leads clean-up in four clicks, repeatable forever.
Home ▸ Remove Rows ▸ Remove Duplicates
On the cleaned column, after lowercasing. Duplicates are case-sensitive here, unlike Excel.
Transform ▸ Replace Values
"Dehra Dun" → "Dehradun". For many spellings, merge with a mapping table instead.
Add Column ▸ Custom Column · Conditional Column · Column From Examples
Calculations and buckets, without M when you can avoid it.

Combine and load

Select columns ▸ Transform ▸ Unpivot Other Columns
Twelve month columns become Month + Value rows. The most useful click in the tool.
Home ▸ Group By
Sum, count, average per key: a pivot that lives in the pipeline.
Home ▸ Merge Queries
A join. Left Outer keeps everything on the left; Inner keeps matches; Left Anti finds orphans. Expand the columns you want.
Home ▸ Append Queries
Stack same-shaped tables: January under December.
Home ▸ Close & Load To…
Table (into a sheet), Connection only (feeds another query), Add to Data Model (for Power Pivot).
Data ▸ Refresh All
Re-runs every step on the new file. Queries & Connections pane shows what ran.
Home ▸ Manage Parameters
The file path or the month as a parameter, so the next person changes one value instead of editing steps.
Applied Steps ▸ click any step
See the data as it was at that point. Delete the step to undo it. Rename steps so the list reads like a recipe.

Charts and conditional formatting

Chart rules

Compare categories → bar (horizontal) or column
Sorted by value, biggest at the top. Twelve stores is a bar chart, never a pie.
Trend over time → line
Months on the x-axis, one line per series, four lines at most.
Actual vs target → clustered column, or column + line
Combo chart: Insert ▸ Combo. Target as a line, actual as columns.
Part of a whole → 100% stacked, or a pie with ≤3 slices
More slices than that: use a sorted bar.
Title = the takeaway
"Kochi is our fastest-growing store", not "Revenue by store". Link the title to a cell for a live number.
Axis starts at zero
Always for columns and bars. A truncated axis turns a 3% gap into a cliff.
One colour plus one highlight
Grey for everything, the accent for the store you're talking about. Direct labels, no legend, no gridlines you don't need.
No 3-D, no shadows, no smoothing
They distort and they date the deck.
Insert ▸ Sparklines
A trend inside a cell, one per row of a scorecard.

Conditional formatting rules

Home ▸ Conditional Formatting ▸ Data Bars
In-cell bars for a ranked list. Set the minimum to 0 in Manage Rules, or short bars lie.
Color Scales
A heat map of a store × month grid. Two-colour scale; three colours only when the middle value means something.
Icon Sets
Three arrows for above / near / below target. Set the thresholds as numbers, not percentiles.
Highlight Cells ▸ Duplicate Values
The fastest duplicate check on a column of IDs.
New Rule ▸ Use a formula: =$H2<$I2
Whole row turns red when actual is below target. Anchor the column with $, leave the row relative, apply to the whole Table.
=AND($Q2="Cancelled", $P2>10000)
Formula rules can test several columns.
Manage Rules ▸ Stop If True · rule order
The first matching rule wins when several overlap. Keep it to three rules per range.

Word and PowerPoint

Word: styles and review

Ctrl+Alt+1 / 2 / 3
Heading 1, 2, 3. Never bold-and-bigger by hand; the Navigation pane and the TOC depend on real headings.
View ▸ Navigation Pane
The document's outline. Drag a heading to move the whole section.
References ▸ Table of Contents
Automatic, from headings. Right-click ▸ Update Field before every send.
Layout ▸ Breaks ▸ Next Page (section break)
Different headers, page numbering or orientation per section. A page break is not a section break.
Insert ▸ Page Number · Header & Footer
"Page X of Y", the document title, the version.
Paste from Excel ▸ Keep Source Formatting / Link
Link when the numbers will change; paste as picture when the layout must not move.
Review ▸ Track Changes (Ctrl+Shift+E) · New Comment (Ctrl+Alt+M)
The review loop. Accept All when the reviewer signs off; never send a document with changes still showing to a client.
Mailings ▸ Start Mail Merge ▸ Select Recipients (Excel) ▸ Insert Merge Field ▸ Finish
One letter per row of a Table. Clean the Excel first: PROPER names, one address column per line.
Review ▸ Editor · Check Accessibility
Run both before a document leaves the team. Alt text on every image.
File ▸ Save As ▸ PDF
What the reader gets. Keep the .docx as the source.

PowerPoint: storyline and master

SCQA
Situation → Complication → Question → Answer. The answer is slide 2, not slide 20.
Action titles
Every title is a full sentence with the claim: "Online is 54% of revenue and growing". Read only the titles: they should be the whole story.
One message per slide
If the title has "and", it's two slides.
View ▸ Slide Master
Fonts, colours, logo, footer once. Edit layouts, not slides. Design ▸ Variants ▸ Colors for the theme palette.
Home ▸ Layout
Apply a master layout instead of drawing boxes. Reset restores it when someone dragged things.
Paste chart ▸ Use Destination Theme & Link Data
The chart updates from Excel. Embed only when the file goes outside.
Table when the reader needs the numbers; chart when they need the shape
A 12-store scorecard is a table with conditional formatting.
Home ▸ Arrange ▸ Align · Distribute · View ▸ Guides
Aligned boxes read as competent. Eyeballing doesn't.
View ▸ Notes Page · Slide Show ▸ Rehearse Timings · Presenter View
Notes are your script. Rehearse once with the clock.
File ▸ Export ▸ PDF · Create a Video
PDF for email; video with narration for the people who missed the meeting.

Outlook, Teams, Forms, Lists and Planner

Outlook and Teams habits

Subject = the ask + the deadline
"Kothrud promo decision needed by Thu 4 pm", not "Update".
First line is the ask (BLUF)
Bottom line up front. Context after, attachment last. Under 120 words.
Never "please do the needful"
Say what the needful is, who does it, by when.
Attach ▸ Share link, not the file
One live copy on SharePoint. The attachment is the version that goes stale.
Search: from:vikram hasattachment:yes received:this week
Operators beat scrolling.
Calendar ▸ Scheduling Assistant · Focus time · Time zones
Invite with an agenda in the body; 25-minute meetings; block two hours a day for real work.
Teams: team ▸ channel ▸ thread
Team = a group of people; channel = a topic; thread = a conversation. Reply in the thread, not as a new post.
@name · @channel
@name for one person's action. @channel only when everyone must read it. Both are a promise of a reply.
Files tab = SharePoint
Every channel file lives in the team's SharePoint site. Edit there; don't download and re-upload.
Meeting ▸ Record · Transcript · Collaborative notes · Loop components
Notes live in the invite; a Loop table of actions updates everywhere it's pasted.
Teams vs email
Teams for the team, in-flight work, quick questions. Email for outside the company, decisions to keep, anything with a CA on copy.

Forms, Lists, Planner

Forms: Choice · Text · Rating · Date · Likert · Net Promoter Score
One question per screen for phones; required only where you'll act on the answer.
Forms ▸ Branching
"If Score ≤ 6, ask why." Set it after all questions exist.
Forms ▸ Settings ▸ One response per person · Record name
Store audits: on. Anonymous NPS: off.
Responses ▸ Open in Excel
The results workbook. Group Forms saves it in SharePoint, where Power Automate can reach it.
Lists: Text · Choice · Date · Person · Number · Lookup · Yes/No
A "Store issues" list. Choice for Status, Person for Owner, Date for Due.
Lists ▸ Create view · Format view · Rules
"Open issues by store" as a saved view; a rule that emails the owner when Status changes.
Planner: Bucket · Task · Label · Assign · Due · Checklist
Buckets by phase or store; one owner per task; labels for priority. Charts view for the status meeting.
Planner ▸ Schedule view · Group by Assigned to
Who is overloaded this week, on one screen.

Power Automate, modelling and Copilot

Power Automate anatomy

Trigger → Condition → Action
Every flow. One trigger; as many actions as needed; conditions branch.
Automated · Instant · Scheduled
Fires on an event (new Forms response); on a button; on a clock (Monday 8 am).
Forms ▸ When a new response is submitted → Get response details
Two steps, always in this order. The first has only the ID.
Excel Online (Business) ▸ Add a row into a table
The file must be in OneDrive/SharePoint and the range must be a Table. The number-one reason a flow fails.
Teams ▸ Post message in a chat or channel
Use dynamic content for the fields; keep the message to three lines.
Approvals ▸ Start and wait for an approval
Discount requests: approver, details, then a Condition on Outcome = Approve.
Recurrence → List rows present in a table → Apply to each → Send an email
The weekly reminder flow. Filter rows with an OData filter to keep the loop small.
formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'dd-MMM-yyyy') · concat(a, ' ', b)
Expressions, under the Expression tab, not typed into the box.
Configure run after ▸ has failed
Error branch: post to Teams when a step fails. Otherwise failures are silent.
Test ▸ Manually · Run history
Test every flow twice before you trust it. Read the inputs and outputs of the failed step.
Don't automate
Anything that runs fewer than four times a year, anything with a judgement call, or anything you can't yet do by hand.

What-If and modelling hygiene

Data ▸ What-If Analysis ▸ Goal Seek
Set cell (the result) to value (the target) by changing cell (one input). "What discount hits ₹50 lakh?"
What-If ▸ Scenario Manager
Base / best / worst as named sets of inputs. Summary report compares them.
What-If ▸ Data Table
One input across the top or two inputs in a grid; the formula in the corner. The sensitivity table for the CFO.
Data ▸ Solver
Maximise or minimise a cell by changing several cells under constraints. Add-in; enable it once.
=PMT(rate/12, n, -principal) · =NPV(rate, flows)+flow0 · =IRR(flows)
Loan instalment; net present value (first flow outside the function); internal rate of return.
Assumptions sheet
Every input in one place, blue font, with a source and a date. Formulas in black. Links from other sheets in green.
No numbers inside formulas
=P2*1.18 is a bug waiting for a GST change. =P2*(1+GSTRate).
A Checks block
Totals tie to the source; sum of parts = whole; no #N/A anywhere: =SUMPRODUCT(--ISERROR(range)) should be 0.
Power Pivot ▸ Manage ▸ Diagram View
Sales to Stores, Products, Targets by key. Measures, not calculated fields: Total Revenue := SUM(Sales[LineRevenue]).

Copilot prompts

Table + grain + filter + output
"Sales table, one row per order line, Status = Delivered, Month 2026-08: LineRevenue by Channel as a 3-row table."
"…and tell me which column you summed"
Makes the mistake visible before you accept it.
"Add a column called … that …"
A formula column you can read and keep. Prefer this to chat answers.
"Use only the figures below; add no others"
For any Word draft. Copilot likes to compute a fourth number from your three.
"Rewrite as three bullets, keep every number unchanged"
Rewrites lose digits. Say so.
"Recap: decisions, owners, dates; quote the speaker"
Teams. Quotes expose mishearings ("fifteen" vs "fifty").
Verify: one SUMIFS per number, on a Checks sheet
Prompt · Copilot's answer · your formula · difference. Nothing reaches a slide without a row here.
Never copy a number out of the chat pane
It was computed once and won't update. Formulas in cells do.

Ten habits that separate a careful analyst from a fast one

  1. Say the grain out loud before you write anything. "One row per order line" stops half of all double-counting; the Sales sheet has 6,314 lines and 3,000 orders.
  2. Press Ctrl+T before the first formula. Tables make references readable, pivots refreshable and flows possible.
  3. Put "Status = Delivered" in every revenue number, in the formula and in the footnote. Cancelled and returned lines are in the same sheet.
  4. Check both ends of every date range. ">="&DATE(2026,8,1) needs its "<="&DATE(2026,8,31). Off-by-a-day is the most common silent error in business reporting.
  5. Never put a figure in a slide that you have not seen at the row level at least once. Drill through the pivot; filter the Table; look at ten rows.
  6. Keep inputs in one place and never inside a formula. A rate, a target, a date lives in a named cell with a source next to it.
  7. Clean into a new column, never over the original. The before and the after are both evidence.
  8. Tie one number to a source you trust before you publish anything new: last month's deck, the finance report, the CA's number.
  9. Write the title as the finding. A chart called "Revenue by store" is unfinished; "Kothrud is ₹46,801 below target" is done.
  10. Name and version the file the way the team can find it: 2026-08_Store-Scorecard_v03.xlsx, on SharePoint, shared as a link. "Final_FINAL2" is how work gets lost.
